applies_to: Carrier 48/50JC 04-06 single-package rooftop units (R-410A) with SystemVu controls, version 4.X.
summary: The 48/50JC small rooftops use the SystemVu unit control, which talks BACnet MS/TP (or CCN) on one RS-485 BMS port. The BACnet table holds about 720 analog, binary and multistate values covering setpoints, sensors, network inputs, runtimes, alerts and configuration.
notes: Taken from Appendix E of the guide (pp. 136-148: AV, BV and MSV tables). MSV objects are listed as MV.
AV 9020 and AV 9021 print their units as 'F; they are listed as °F.
The table also gives a CCN point name for most objects; only the BACnet side is captured here.

Value ranges from the table are added to the descriptions in brackets. The BACnet table prints no multistate state texts; the display and CCN tables elsewhere in the guide list the options for many of them.
The guide also lists about 14 string objects (software versions, model and serial numbers, device description), all with the ID String:0; they are left out because no usable instance is printed.
Which objects exist depends on unit size, heat type and installed options (economizer, Humidi-MiZer, VFD fan, accessories). Many alert and fault flags (a_*, f_*) are printed as R/W and kept that way.

source.title: 48/50JC 04-06 Ultra High Efficiency Single Package Rooftop Units with SystemVu Controls Version 4.X, Controls, Start-Up, Operation and Troubleshooting (Appendix E: BACnet Points List)

integration.summary: The SystemVu control has one RS-485 BMS port. Set BAS Protocol to BACnet on the unit display (Settings > Network Settings), set the MAC address and baud rate, power-cycle and connect to the MS/TP trunk. Run occupancy from a BACnet schedule or the BMS Occupancy Request point, write the occupied setpoints, and read the system mode, temperatures and the active fault count.

minimum_points.why: Occupancy request from the BMS (unocc / occupied / disabled)

minimum_points.name: sys_mode
minimum_points.why: Current mode (off, cool, heat, vent, test)

minimum_points.name: req_fan_spd
minimum_points.why: Indoor fan speed the control is calling for, %

integration.enable: Set BAS Protocol Select to BACnet on the unit display (Settings > Network Settings > BAS Protocol; default None). With BACnet selected the local occupancy schedule is reset and scheduling comes from the BACnet side: a BACnet schedule, or the BMS Occupancy Request (MV 12; the display tables list Unocc, Occupied and Disabled). Unit Control Type (MV 2) decides whether the unit runs from thermostat inputs or a space sensor.
integration.heartbeat: Network Input Timeout (AV 9089, default 30 min per the display tables) applies to the network input values. The guide does not say what the unit does when it expires, so keep any written network value refreshed well inside that time.
integration.remote_sensors: Writable network inputs exist for space temperature (Network Space Temp Value, AV 7006), outdoor air temperature (AV 7007), return air temperature (AV 7005), space RH (AV 376), outdoor RH (AV 7003), IAQ and OAQ CO2 (AV 7001, AV 7002) and OA cfm (AV 371). The guide doesn't explain how the unit picks a network value over a local sensor; check the sensor channel settings on the display. The 'BACnet device for ...' and 'Object instance for ...' AVs let the unit read a sensor from another BACnet device.
setup: BACnet MS/TP only, on the single RS-485 BMS port that is also used for CCN. Defaults: MAC address 01, baud 76800 (BACNET BAUDRATE 4).
i-Vu auto ID: with the auto ID scheme on, set the MAC and the device ID becomes the network number plus the MAC. With it off, set the MAC and write the device ID over BACnet; the controller keeps it.
To set the device ID by hand, set BACnet ID to manual on the display and enter it there. The MAC range for each mode is in the guide's BACnet settings table.
Power the controller down after changing the BACnet settings, then connect it to the MS/TP network.
gotchas: Instances are not sequential (AV 9089, BV 7048, MV 2002 and so on); map by instance, not by position in the table.
Many configuration MVs and AVs are option codes or sensor channel numbers; read the current value and check the display before writing.
The guide gives only a numeric range for MV 12 and the other multistates; confirm the state numbering on the unit before writing.
BV 7048 shows the alarm relay; which alerts drive the relay is set under Unit Configurations > Alarm Relay.
